title: Onfrey and Duran band and Maurice Duran
summary: Russell asks about bands of Coochie Martin's era; Kimball recalls Onfrey and Duran; news of Maurice Duran's death.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Oh, one other question, too, while I think of it, uh, Coochie Martin, which band was your father playing in at that time? Do you remember, was that, did Coochie Martin play with Robichoke too? I don't remember much about it. No.
They're all dead, I guess, in the Martin family. There was a band that was named Onfrey and Duran.
By the way, I heard just yesterday or the day before that he died in California. Is that right?

He had been here a year or so ago, his father had been sick, still living down in the ninth ward, uh, the Zardy Street. I met him in California, and I met him here years ago. So, uh, I guess it must be true, two different people told me they heard from California these guys.
It was, uh, called Onfrey and Duran, Willie Onfrey, the clarinet player.
The old man, not, not the Willie. No, no.
The Willie, he was the youngster then.
And, uh, Duran, and Johnny St. Cyr, and, uh, Coochie Martin. No, not Coochie Martin, he wasn't in that group. I don't remember what group.
But your father worked with them then? Yes, he worked with them. And, uh, and, uh, well, you, uh, I interrupted you were going to tell about your first instrument and all your guitar and the band.
